<STRUCT_0001>
In this section we explain a general procedure for producing the
sites we will be working with. This discussion will make little or
no sense unless the reader has read
Topologies, Section <REF_0001>.

<STRUCT_0002><STRUCT_0003>
Let <MATH_0001> be a base scheme.
Take any category <MATH_0002> constructed as in
Sets, Lemma <REF_0002> starting with
<MATH_0003> and any set of schemes over <MATH_0004> you want to be included.
Choose any set of
coverings <MATH_0005> on <MATH_0006> as in
Sets, Lemma <REF_0003>
starting with the category <MATH_0007> and the class of fppf
coverings. Let <MATH_0008> denote the big fppf site so
obtained, and let <MATH_0009> denote the corresponding
big fppf site of <MATH_0010>. (The above is entirely as prescribed in Topologies,
Section <REF_0004>.)

<STRUCT_0004><STRUCT_0005>
Given choices as above the category of algebraic spaces over <MATH_0011>
has a set of isomorphism classes. One way to see this is to use the
fact that any algebraic space over <MATH_0012> is of the form <MATH_0013> for
some <ACCENT_0001>tale equivalence relation <MATH_0014> with
<MATH_0015>, see
Spaces, Lemma <REF_0005>.
Hence we can find a full subcategory <MATH_0016> of the category of
algebraic spaces over <MATH_0017> which has a set of objects
such that each algebraic space is isomorphic to an object of
<MATH_0018>. We fix a choice of such a category.

<STRUCT_0006><STRUCT_0007>
In the sections below, given a topology <MATH_0019>, the big site
<MATH_0020> (resp.<SPACE_0001>the big site <MATH_0021>
of an algebraic space <MATH_0022> over <MATH_0023>)
has as underlying category the category <MATH_0024>
(resp.<SPACE_0002>the subcategory <MATH_0025> of <MATH_0026>, see
Categories, Example <REF_0006>).
The procedure for turning this into a site is as usual by defining a
class of <MATH_0027>-coverings and using
Sets, Lemma <REF_0007>
to choose a sufficiently large set of coverings which defines the topology.

<STRUCT_0008><STRUCT_0009>
We point out that the <TEXTITOPEN_0001>small <ACCENT_0002>tale site <MATH_0028>
of an algebraic space <MATH_0029><TEXTITCLOSE_0001> has already been defined in
Properties of Spaces, Definition
<REF_0008>.
Its objects are schemes <ACCENT_0003>tale over <MATH_0030>, of which there are plenty
by definition of an algebraic spaces. However,
a more natural site, from the perspective of this chapter (compare
Topologies, Definition <REF_0009>)
is the site <MATH_0031> of
Properties of Spaces, Definition
<REF_0010>.
These two sites define the same topos, see
Properties of Spaces, Lemma <REF_0011>.
We will not redefine these in this chapter; instead we will simply
use them.
